summary: Modular monolith architecture combining React (Vite) frontend and FastAPI backend with PostgreSQL hosted on On-Premise Server (Docker Compose / Podman). Estimated monthly infrastructure cost ranges from $15 to $60.

frontend.justification: Lightweight client-rendered SPA provides rapid interactive state management with minimal framework overhead.

alternatives.why_not: Server-side rendering runtime unnecessary for authenticated, non-SEO internal/SaaS app.

tradeoffs: Initial bundle download before client hydration.

backend.justification: Asynchronous Python framework with automatic OpenAPI documentation and Pydantic validation; enables rapid MVP development.

alternatives.why_not: FastAPI is more lightweight, provides native async performance, and integrates better with mobile APIs.

tradeoffs: Requires explicit worker process management (Uvicorn / Gunicorn) for multi-core scaling.

database.justification: Self-hosted PostgreSQL container with local persistent volumes, preserving zero-cloud dependency for on-premise deployment.

alternatives.why_not: Public cloud managed databases violate strict on_premise boundaries.

tradeoffs: Requires connection pooling (e.g. PgBouncer) under high concurrent connection spikes.

hosting.justification: Strict on-premise corporate datacenter constraint strictly eliminates external public cloud PaaS/SaaS dependencies; containers orchestrated locally on bare-metal or hypervisor VMs.

alternatives.why_not: Public cloud services violate the mandatory on_premise isolation boundary.
Kubernetes introduces immense operational complexity and dedicated DevOps staffing burden compared to Docker Compose / Podman for on-prem operations.

tradeoffs: Requires physical hardware procurement, manual OS patching, and internal disaster recovery planning.

supporting.justification: Bi-directional WebSocket communication enabling real-time chat, notifications, and collaborative state syncing.

alternatives.why_not: Proprietary commercial SaaS with steep pricing jumps under high concurrency.

tradeoffs: Requires stateful connection management on backend workers.

supporting.justification: High-performance S3-compatible object storage deployed inside on-premise infrastructure without external internet connectivity.

alternatives.why_not: Public cloud storage violates strict on_premise isolation boundary.

tradeoffs: Requires local disk storage capacity alerting.

supporting.justification: Authentication service resolving email_password requirements with secure token issuance.

alternatives.why_not: Cloud SaaS identity providers require public internet access, violating on-premise / air-gapped isolation.

tradeoffs: Self-managed Keycloak database realm backups required.

supporting.justification: Open-source AMQP message broker deployed on-premise for reliable asynchronous decoupling without cloud connectivity.

alternatives.why_not: Amazon SQS is a public cloud service unavailable in air-gapped or on-prem environments.

tradeoffs: Requires persistent disk volume monitoring and clustering setup.

assumptions: Estimates based on published cloud pricing units and standard resource allocations.
